blocks.text: Lesson 9 — Evidence, severity, disclosure and professional reports

LEARNING OUTCOME
Write reproducible findings with evidence, impact, remediation and safe retest steps.

Safety rule: work only with devices, accounts and training applications you own or have explicit written permission to assess. Use synthetic information. A public system or a suspicious person is not permission.

A finding includes a clear title, affected asset, severity rationale, confidence, business impact, prerequisites, safe reproduction, evidence reference, remediation and retest checklist. Report what evidence proves; do not infer who is responsible from one log entry or IP address.

blocks.text: Collect the minimum needed, preserve timestamps, restrict access and redact secrets and personal data. Never publish scan output or screenshots online. Follow the owner’s retention and deletion process.

blocks.caption: Visual 3/6 — Impact. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.
Visual 4/6 — Evidence. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.

blocks.text: Use the designated contact or disclosure channel, agree on timelines and avoid threatening public disclosure. Retest only within the authorized scope and mark the issue fixed, partially fixed or unresolved.

blocks.caption: Visual 5/6 — Remediation. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.
Visual 6/6 — Retest result. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.

blocks.text: Practice checklist: (1) read the lab rules, (2) use fabricated data or an isolated training target, (3) predict what the control should do, (4) test one small condition, (5) save only minimal evidence, and (6) explain the defensive follow-up. Stop and ask the owner if any target or action is outside the approved scope.

blocks.output: Protect the report and exclude real secrets.

blocks.question: Before Lesson 9 testing, what should be confirmed?
options: The exact target is covered by written permission
A friend said it is okay
blocks.explanation: Written permission should define target and allowed methods.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: How should a finding from Lesson 9 be handled?
options: Include a real password as proof
Save minimal redacted evidence and report through the approved channel
blocks.explanation: Findings need scoped, protected and reproducible evidence.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What requires the learner to stop?
options: A lab result needs an explanation
Target is out of scope or testing may cause unexpected harm
blocks.explanation: Stop if scope or safety limits may be crossed.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What is a sound step after applying a fix?
options: Retest the same authorized condition and document the result
blocks.explanation: Retesting verifies the correction and preserves a useful record.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What should happen when a target is outside scope?
options: Stop and ask the owner to clarify permission
blocks.explanation: Scope is a boundary; do not proceed without permission.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.
